newsitem.title: CHINA: Dickson to boost outlets, signs franchises.
newsitem.headline: Dickson to boost outlets, signs franchises.

text.p: Dickson Concepts (International) Ltd said on Wednesday it intends to open about 100 new shops internationally during the current financial year.

Chairman Dickson Poon told a news conference the retailer has also signed a franchise agreement with Brooks Brothers, a wholly owned unit of Marks and Spencer Plc, to exclusively operate Brooks Brothers stores in South East Asia.
He said Dickson Concepts has also entered into an exclusive long-term agreement with Coach, a division of Sara Lee Corp, to distribute Coach merchandise in South East Asia, commencing on September 1.

"Given the development and growth of existing brands, together with the acquisition of franchising rights for new brands such as Brooks Brothers and Coach, the group intends to open approximately 100 shops on an international basis during the current financial year, taking the group's worldwide retail network to more than 350," Dickson Concepts said in a statement.
It said it expected at least 20 Brooks Brothers franchise stores to be opened in South East Asia over the next two years, with the first stores scheduled to open in 1998.
The Brooks Brothers label offers a range of men's and women's business and casual wear, leather goods and accessories.

Dickson Concepts said that it planned to open 29 Coach retail locations in Hong Kong, Taiwan and Singapore. It said the figure included opening 16 new Coach shops and assuming the operation of 13 existing retail locations in these markets.
"In addition, Dickson Concepts and Coach will launch Coach in China and explore further expansion opportunities in Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia," it said.

Coach offers a range of quality leather goods for men and women. A new menswear line was recently launched. Worldwide sales of Coach merchandise in 1996 exceeded US$500 million, Dickson Concepts said.
Dickson Concepts said its Paris listed subsidiary S.T. Dupont had signed a worldwide licence agreement with Inter Parfums to develop and distribute S.T. Dupont perfume lines.
The agreement covers both men's and women's fragrances and the first men's fragrance is expected to be launched within the next 12 to 18 months, Dickson Concepts said.
It said Inter Parfums was committed to spending a minimum of HK$123 million during the first three years on advertising and promotion.

Dickson Concept also said it had reached an understanding with Ferrari S.p.A. to explore the development of retailing concepts for the brand name "Ferrari", which has been a legend in the world of motor racing for over fifty years.
"It is intended that a retailing concept be developed around the Ferrari spirit which will combine a complete retailing offering of lifestyle merchandise and interactive atractions," Poon said.
This new concept in retailing was expected to be lauched initially with the opening of flagship stores in New York, London, Tokyo and Hong Kong, he added.
